newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines cut off-peak summer fares.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines cut off-peak summer fares.

text.p: Several U.S. airlines said they cut off-peak summer fares for domestic flights up to 45 percent, following a move by American Airlines.
AMR Corp's American Airlines and American Eagle said Thursday they will offer 45 percent fare cuts during off-peak summer periods on domestic flights.

The fares will average 45 percent off the regular 21-day advance purchase fares but will require only a seven-day advance purchase, the airlines said. Tickets must be bought by June 16 for flights through the end of October.
American said it will offer special prices on flights to Mexico, Russia, Brussels and St. Croix in the Caribbean.
On Friday, Continental Airlines Inc said it matched the fare sale in markets where it competes with American.
US Airways Group Inc said it reduced its summer off-peak fares up to 45 percent in more than 6,000 markets in the United States and Canada. Roundtrip fares start at $105, the airline said.
Delta Air Lines Inc, Northwest Airlines Corp and UAL Corp's United Airlines did not return calls seeking comment.
